title: Enterprise Onboarding + Support & Escalation Playbook (Integration, Known Issues, Health Checks & QBR)
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures and templates for enterprise customer onboarding at Redwood Inference, including the integration checklist, escalation paths, common known issues & workarounds, recommended day-1 support processes, health checks, and a QBR template. The audience is Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and the SRE/Platform teams supporting enterprise accounts.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers by providing a repeatable onboarding sequence.
- Provide clear escalation matrices and SLAs so support and engineering can respond predictably.
- Enable data-driven QBRs and health checks to retain and grow accounts.

Owner and Stakeholders:
- Document owner: Customer Success (Priya Desai)
- Primary stakeholders: CSMs, Solutions Engineering, Support, Eng-SRE, Eng-Platform, Product
- Technical escalation owners: Eng-SRE (pager), Eng-Serving-Runtime (performance regressions)

Scope:
This playbook applies to all enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments and Hosted accounts with enterprise contracts. It covers onboarding through the first 90 days and standard recurring health checks and QBR cadence after onboarding.

High-Level Onboarding Phases (90-day structure):
1. Pre-sales-to-onboard handoff (Day 0-7)
   - Deliverables: Welcome packet, account contacts, security questionnaire, prelim capacity plan.
2. Deployment & Integration (Day 1-21)
   - Deliverables: API keys, networking config (VPC peering / Private), test dataset, initial throughput test.
3. Validation & Performance Tuning (Day 7-45)
   - Deliverables: Baseline latency/cost dashboard, quantization/recommendation report, cache/batching config.
4. Production Launch & Burn-in (Day 30-90)
   - Deliverables: SLA adherence report, incident response runbook, run rate-based sizing recommendation.

Detailed Onboarding Checklist (Integration focus):
- Preboarding (CSM / SE):
  - Confirm signed contract and billing contact.
  - Confirm compliance requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI, data residency).
  - Identify technical contacts and stakeholder map.
- Networking & Security (for Private/Dedicated):
  - Provide VPC peering instructions and required CIDR ranges.
  - Collect KMS/HSM integration details if provided.
  - Exchange public keys for audit logging endpoints.
- Credentials & Access:
  - Provision API keys (scoped) and temporary admin tokens.
  - Configure RBAC roles and owner/team access.
- Integration Tests (SE / Customer):
  - Run basic API smoke tests: POST /v1/generate and POST /v1/embeddings.
  - Verify streaming and function-calling flows with a sample conversation.
  - Validate response formats for structured outputs (JSONSchema).
- Performance Baseline:
  - Execute synthetic load: 1000 small requests, 100 long-context requests; collect P50/P95/P99 latency and token cost.
  - Record KV cache hit rate and batching efficiency.
- Observability & Alerts:
  - Configure dashboards (latency/token cost/error rates) in Redwood Console.
  - Ensure alerting: error rate > 1% for 5m, P95 latency > 800ms, cost-per-1k-tokens > budget threshold.
- Go-live checklist:
  - Final sign-off from SE, SRE, and customer security.
  - Agreed rollback policy and fallback model mapping.

Integration Guide (step-by-step):
1. Network prep
   - Ensure outbound connectivity to api.redwood.ai and collect IP allowlist if customer requires.
   - For Private deployments, follow reference-architecture: subnets for inference workers, control plane egress, and audit-logging collector.
2. Auth and RBAC
   - Create scoped API key: role=ingest-only, expires=30d (demo).
   - Map customer teams to RBAC groups in Console: engineers, analytics, security.
3. Sample curl tests
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Hello"}'
4. Observability setup
   - Import dashboard JSON (appendix A) into Console dashboards.
   - Configure SLOs in team workspace: latency P95 < 1s; availability 99.9%.

Escalation Matrix and Procedures:
- First-line support (L1): Customer Success & Support Engineers (business hours)
  - SLA: respond within 1 business hour for Sev 2, 15 minutes for Sev 1 (pager).
- L2: Support Engineering / Solutions Engineering
  - SLA: 2 hours for root-cause triage on Sev 1, 24 hours for Sev 3 issues.
- L3: Eng-SRE and Eng-Serving-Runtime (on-call rotation)
  - Pager for Sev 1 (system outage affecting >25% requests or sustained >5m latency degradation).

Escalation contact table (use PagerDuty & email in parallel):
| Severity | Customer Impact | Primary Contact | Backup Contact | Expected Response |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Sev 1 | Platform unavailable or critical regression | eng-sre-pager@redwood.ai (PD) | oncall-serving@redwood.ai | 15 minutes |
| Sev 2 | Degraded performance for a customer, partial outage | support@redwood.ai (L1) / SE | eng-sre (PD) | 1 hour |
| Sev 3 | Minor functional issue or integration bug | support@redwood.ai | CSM | 24 hours |

Escalation steps (numbered):
1. L1 triage: reproduce with customer, collect logs + request ID, gather environment details, set temporary mitigation if available.
2. If L1 cannot mitigate within SLA, escalate to L2 with collected artifacts and hypothesis.
3. L2 performs deeper triage; if root cause is platform or infra, escalate to L3 (Eng-SRE).
4. L3 engages code owners and decides on mitigation (hotfix, rollback, capacity increase).
5. Communication: CSM updates customer every 30 minutes for Sev 1 until resolved.

Runbook: Common Severity 1 Playbook (summary):
- Trigger condition: whole-region latency > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes OR error rate > 5% across customer traffic.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Post to incident channel: #inc-<customer>-sev1 with subject + short description.
  2. Collect: request IDs, sample traces, runtime metric snapshot (last 15m).
  3. Scale up Dedicated pool or route traffic to fallback model variant.
  4. If mitigation fails in 15m, declare incident in Status page and engage exec on-call.

Known Issues & Workarounds (living list):
- Issue 1: High memory usage during long-context inference with model X (v1.2.0)
  - Symptoms: OOM in worker logs after ~8k tokens.
  - Workaround: Limit max_context_length to 6k, enable kv-cache pruning (config: kv_prune_interval=1000), or switch to quantized variant model-x-8bit.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime
- Issue 2: Streaming responses appear truncated for some clients
  - Symptoms: Client SDK fails to reassemble SSE chunks when connection drops briefly.
  - Workaround: Advise customers to enable automatic retry-on-chunk-failure at the SDK level and set keepalive interval to 15s. Sample patch available in SDK guide (appendix B).
  - Owner: eng-developer-experience
- Issue 3: Nondeterministic hallucination spike after new model rollout
  - Symptoms: Increased semantic drift in specific prompt-set; higher manual eval failure rate.
  - Workaround: Immediate rollback to previous verified model variant and open a regression triage ticket; add model to canary with 5% traffic and expanded eval prompt sets.
  - Owner: applied-ml-and-evals

Support Process (day-to-day):
- Ticketing flow:
  - All customer issues go into Zendesk with priority mapping: Sev 1=Urgent, Sev 2=High, Sev3=Normal.
  - Tickets must include reproducible steps, request IDs, and environment.
- Knowledge base:
  - Link KB articles in ticket responses; add new articles for recurring issues.
- Escalation handoff notes:
  - Every escalation must include a one-paragraph summary: what happened, actions taken, why escalated, and outstanding hypothesis.

Health Checks and QBR (templates & cadence):
- 30/60/90-day checks during onboarding:
  - 30-day: integration complete, baseline metrics documented, initial risk items logged.
  - 60-day: throughput tests passed, latency goals met, first incidents resolved < SLA.
  - 90-day: production launch sign-off and cost/performance optimization recommendations delivered.
- Recurring health checks (monthly):
  - Automated report contents: request volume, error rates, P50/P95/P99 latency, token spend trend, KV cache hit rate, model variant % traffic.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template (high level):
  1. Executive summary (1 slide): health status, NPS / satisfaction signals, renewal recommendation.
  2. Metrics (2-3 slides): traffic growth, latency, errors, cost-per-1M tokens trend.
  3. Reliability & Incidents (1 slide): postmortems since last QBR, open action items.
  4. Roadmap & Ask (1 slide): upcoming features or infra changes that impact customer; ask for access or resources if needed.
  5. Optimization opportunities (1 slide): batching/caching/quantization suggestions with projected $/month savings.
  6. Action items & owners (table).

QBR Example Action Items table (text form):
| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Enable KV prefix caching for high-volume route | SE Team | 2026-06-10 | Proposed |
| Add canary for model-v2 rollout | Applied ML | 2026-05-20 | In progress |

Appendices:
A. Dashboard JSON import (link) - include dashboard JSON file in customer workspace: redwood-console/dashboards/customer-<id>/baseline.json
B. SDK retry snippet (javascript) - sample code to safely stream and reassemble events:
   - const stream = client.stream({ model: 'redwood-1' });
   - stream.on('data', chunk => accumulate(chunk));
   - stream.on('error', err => retryWithBackoff());
C. Sample run commands for synthetic testing:
   - k6 script: k6 run --vus 50 --duration 5m synthetic-load.js
D. Contact & escalation directory:
   - support@redwood.ai (L1 responses)
   - se-team@redwood.ai (account SEs)
   - eng-sre-pager@redwood.ai (PagerDuty)

Maintenance and Updates to this Playbook:
- Frequency: Reviewed quarterly by Customer Success & SE; major updates after any Sev 1 related to onboarding or integration flows.
- Change process: PR in confluence doc repo, reviewers: product manager, eng-sre, applied-ml, privacy/security.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft (Priya Desai)
